Hi Alice — great meeting, thanks for the clear summary. Quick responses inline and a couple of anchors to use for modeling.

1) $/1M tokens (private/VPC) — ballpark anchors for modeling:
   - Conservative (QA + stable prod workloads): $700 per 1M tokens
   - Mid (typical production mix with batching & KV cache): $900 per 1M tokens
   - Aggressive (high optimization, long-range caching, large batch ops): $1,150 per 1M tokens

   These assume Redwood Private deployed in your VPC with our private control plane and a usage-based billing layer. Token unit economics depend strongly on average sequence length and KV cache hit rate — if you can share sample prompt/response lengths we can tighten the anchor.

2) Licensing models we recommend (options):
   - Per-environment license + usage (simpler for customers with clear env separation): a fixed environment fee (example: $8k/month/env baseline) + per-1M token usage.
   - Reserved GPU pool (capacity-first): monthly reserved capacity (example: $X GPU nodes priced in slab tiers) + metered token rates below a commit threshold.
   - Hybrid: small environment fee to keep routing/namespace isolation + a committed token tier with overage pricing.

   For your case (3 envs with staging ~= prod), most customers choose either the Per-environment license or Hybrid model. If staging must mirror prod (capacity), we typically recommend modeling it as a full environment for licensing and capacity planning.

3) Support tiers & quick deltas:
   - Standard (business hours, email + ticketing): included in base license.
   - Enterprise (24/7 on-call, named SE, extended retention for logs, annual SOC2 evidence bundle): typically +20–40% on top of base licensing depending on SLA.
   - Managed Ops (dedicated runbook + server-side runbooks + quarterly on-site/remote reviews): custom pricing.

4) I've uploaded a redacted pricing workbook and a short SOW draft to the shared folder. See the attached spreadsheet for an initial private-pricing-grid.xlsx.

Preliminary econ example (for modeling):
- 3 envs: 3 * $8,000 = $24k/month base env fees
- Usage: assume 120M tokens/month at mid anchor ($900/1M) = $108k/month
- Total model = ~$132k/month (~$1.584M/year) — this is a quick illustrative model.

I'll loop in Karthik to validate sizing assumptions for reserved GPU pools if you'd like a capacity-first quote. If your procurement needs a two-line quote (license + usage) we can produce that by EOD next week.

Attached: private-pricing-grid.xlsx (stub)

Hi Alice — quick note from my side on support/contract considerations.

- Support tier recommendation: Given you need SOC2 evidence and production SLAs, I recommend Enterprise support. Typical uplift is ~30% and includes: named technical lead, 4-hour severity 1 SLA, and quarterly security reviews.
- Licensing nuance: if procurement prefers OPEX-only flow we can structure the env fees as monthly operating charges; if they prefer a committed CAPEX/annual model we can convert base env fees into an annual commitment with a discount (5–12% depending on term).
- If you expect staging to be load-testing heavy and mirror prod, count it as a full environment for pricing and capacity planning. That will be the primary driver of the capacity/commit line.

If you can confirm: 1) target anchor to model (pick one of the three Ava listed), 2) whether procurement wants OPEX vs annual commit, and 3) who should receive the formal quote (Jorge or procurement@medsys.com), we will generate a two-line quote + SOW and route through contracts for signature.

Cheers,
